For citizens of exempt countries, stays for these purposes can be visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period; the exemption may also depend on the passport.
Generally, for a stay of more than three months that requires a permit, the application must be submitted to the police commissioner within eight working days of entry.
When a permit is required, the general deadline is eight working days from entry, not thirty. Some short stays are exempt from the permit requirement.
Irregular entry can take place by sea, land or air. The predominance of the sea route stated by the quiz depends on the period and data considered: it is not a permanent rule.
The expression refers to entry into a country without complying with its legal conditions. It should not be confused with a stay that becomes irregular after an initially lawful entry.
Facilitating irregular entry can be linked to human trafficking and labor exploitation, but not every irregular migrant is a victim of trafficking.

The quiz considers it false to identify the Tyrrhenian coast as a main entry route: the routes identified include the central and eastern Mediterranean and the overland Balkan route. Routes can change over time.
A lawful entry does not become illegal simply because the person lacks permanent residence. Their status may subsequently become irregular, for example when their authorized stay expires.

In the specified cases of refusal of entry, the carrier must take charge of the person and return them to the country they came from or the country that issued their travel document, not to the prefecture.

The quiz indicates VERO because criminal networks may facilitate irregular entry and exploit people. However, the wording is too broad: irregular immigration does not always involve trafficking or exploitation, which are distinct from migrant smuggling.
Lampedusa and Pantelleria have been affected by sea routes towards Sicily. The importance of individual routes changes over time.
Apulia has experienced arrivals by sea, including along the Adriatic route. The relative importance of individual areas varies over time, and the quiz does not specify the comparison period.

The quiz indicates VERO, referring to crossings in Friuli Venezia Giulia as possible points of entry by land. Routes vary over time: the ministry source identifies the region's border as being on the Balkan route, without establishing a permanent ranking of individual crossings.
The Ionian coast of Calabria has seen landings, for example at Roccella Ionica. The relative importance of routes changes over time.
Gorizia lies along the eastern border, which has experienced irregular entries by land. The intensity of flows can change over time.

The quiz considers it false to identify Rome and Fregene as a main point of entry: the routes identified by the Ministry include sea routes to the south and the overland Balkan route. The distribution of arrivals can change.

The quiz indicates FALSO, but the answer depends on the period and the criterion used: Sardinia also records landings and is reached by a central Mediterranean route. It cannot be ruled out entirely as a landing area.

The quiz considers it false to identify Milan as a main point of entry: the routes identified concern borders and arrival coasts. Milan is an inland city and may instead be a place of transit or a destination.

The quiz considers it false to identify the western Ligurian coast as a main point of entry: the routes identified include the central and eastern Mediterranean and the overland Balkan route. Routes can change over time.

The quiz considers it false to identify Versilia as a main point of entry: the routes identified include the central and eastern Mediterranean and the overland Balkan route. Routes can change over time.

Facilitating illegal entry can result in imprisonment and confiscation of the vehicle used for the offense. The sentence depends on the offense and circumstances: the reference to 15 years does not describe every case, nor does any assistance automatically constitute the offense.
Italian rules on the entry of foreign nationals generally apply to non-EU nationals and stateless persons. Irregular entry means failing to comply with the applicable entry conditions.
Article 10-bis establishes an offence for entry or stay in breach of the specified provisions, punishable by a fine; specific exceptions and conditions apply.
The general immigration rules for foreign nationals apply to non-EU nationals and stateless persons; an EU citizen does not become an irregular immigrant merely by failing to carry a document.

It is not just a matter of a warning: entry or stay in breach of the specified provisions may constitute the offence punishable by a fine under Article 10-bis, subject to the conditions and exceptions set out in law.

Not all risks can be ruled out: criminal networks that organize irregular entry can threaten security and exploit the people they transport. This does not mean that everyone who entered irregularly is dangerous.

Irregular stay can lead to expulsion, but not automatically whenever a permit expires: the law specifies conditions and safeguards, including the case of a permit that expired more than sixty days ago without an application for renewal.

Having no permit or an expired permit does not result in immediate regularization. In cases provided for by law, expulsion may instead be ordered, taking account of the applicable conditions and safeguards.
The acts of facilitating entry specified by law carry prison sentences and fines; in the specified cases, the vehicle used for the offence is also confiscated.
Facilitating irregular entry, in the cases specified in Article 12, is an offence punishable by imprisonment among other penalties, not merely an administrative violation.

The driver must implement and document vehicle security measures: failures to do so may result in penalties. The verdict is general: ‘incontrovertible evidence’ is not always required, and criminal liability does not automatically follow from the mere presence of hidden people.

The company must also organize effective measures to prevent unauthorized access and may be penalized for its own failures. The verdict is general: the mere lack of ‘incontrovertible evidence’ does not automatically establish criminal liability.
For transport to the United Kingdom, companies and drivers must apply an effective system to prevent unauthorized access to vehicles. Checks and records help demonstrate the measures taken.
The driver is not necessarily the only person liable. For example, under the British civil penalty system the vehicle owner may also be liable; criminal liability requires a separate assessment.
Liability is not limited to the driver. For example, under the British civil penalty system the vehicle owner may also be liable; criminal liability requires a separate assessment.
Confiscation of the vehicle does not rule out a prison sentence: the law also provides for imprisonment for the acts of facilitation specified in Article 12.
The penalties for facilitation do not apply exclusively to the driver: the rule applies to anyone who commits the punishable acts specified by law.
Facilitating irregular entry is an offence in the cases specified by law: it carries not only a financial penalty but also imprisonment.

A carrier may be held liable for participating in the facilitation of illegal entry. However, the reference to mere knowledge is general: knowing about the transport does not automatically amount to committing the offence; conduct and the other legal requirements must be established.
The law punishes those who commit the acts specified in Article 12 that are aimed at procuring illegal entry. Liability must be established according to the conditions of that provision.

A special customs regime does not make cargo immune from checks: during operations and under the conditions provided for by law, the police may inspect vehicles and the goods carried if there are reasonable grounds related to the specified offences.
The law does not merely penalize irregular entry or stay: it also provides penalties for those who commit the acts specified in Article 12 that are aimed at procuring illegal entry.

The carrier's obligations are also laid down by Italian law, not only by bilateral agreements with the country of origin: the carrier must check the required documents and report the presence of people on board in an irregular situation to the border police.

The law requires the carrier to check the documents required for entry, not to personally verify that the traveller has sufficient financial means. The latter is a separate entry condition checked by the authorities.
An air, sea or land carrier must check that the foreign national being transported has the documents required to enter Italian territory.

The quiz indicates VERO, but the rule places the obligation on the carrier, not the vehicle, when a person must be refused entry. The specified destination is the country of departure or the country that issued the travel document, not necessarily the one on the ticket.

The carrier must check the required documents and report irregularities to the border police. A breach carries a financial penalty; in more serious cases it may also result in suspension or revocation of the authorization.

For entry into Italy, the carrier must check that the foreign national being transported has the required documents. The check concerns entry documents, not an independent assessment of the right to stay.
A carrier that brought a person refused entry to the border must immediately take responsibility for them and return them to the country of departure or the country that issued the travel document.

Breaching the duties to check and report carries a financial penalty; in more serious cases the law also provides for suspension or revocation of the authorization relating to the activity and the vehicle.
Reporting the presence of foreign nationals in an irregular situation to the border police is a legal obligation of the carrier, not an offence of informing on someone.
This is not merely a recommendation: the carrier is obliged to report to the border police any foreign nationals on board who are in an irregular situation.
Heartbeat detectors look for the small vibrations produced by a heartbeat and can help locate people hidden in vehicles.
Locking the vehicle and parking in a monitored area reduces opportunities for unauthorized access; after the stop, the locks must also be checked to ensure they are intact.
A thorough check of the vehicle and any trailer can detect unauthorized access and hidden people, including in areas not visible from the driver's seat.
The check described in the references uses carbon dioxide detectors, not oxygen detectors: the probe measures CO₂ that can build up from breathing.

The quiz indicates FALSO, but the wording is ambiguous: a carrier may be required to check passengers' documents for international transport. Physical checks of the vehicle are also needed to prevent hidden access; checking passengers' documents alone is not enough.
Passive millimetre-wave systems produce images that can help identify people who may be hidden in vehicles, without emitting radiation.
A heartbeat detector uses sensors on the vehicle to detect vibrations associated with a hidden person.
Probes measure carbon dioxide in the air inside the compartment: an increase may indicate the presence of people breathing.
Gamma-ray scanning has been used to search for people hidden in vehicles. Its use depends on local rules: in France, for example, it is not permitted when people are suspected to be present.
Dog teams can help officers detect people hidden in a vehicle, alongside other inspection methods.
The WWW is an internet service, not a type of radiation that makes it possible to see inside vehicles. Inspection tools include heartbeat detectors.
The inspection looks for hidden people, for example using heartbeat detectors or dog teams; it does not involve forcing them out with high-frequency sound waves.
Checks for people on board are carried out on the vehicle, for example through inspections and heartbeat detectors, not normally by observing its interior via satellite.
The checks are intended to locate hidden people using inspections and detection equipment, not explosive charges designed to frighten them.
Completely unloading the goods is not inevitable: external checks and instruments such as CO₂ probes can detect signs of people without unloading everything.
Monitoring and securing the vehicle, especially in risk areas, limits opportunities for unauthorized access; checks must also be carried out after stops.
The vulnerable parts of the vehicle must be checked, and the competent authorities notified immediately if unauthorized access is suspected.
People can hide in places other than the cargo compartment: the check also covers the roof, interior, area behind the cab and axles.
When transporting passengers, the interior must also be checked, because an unauthorized person may be among the legitimate passengers.
Damage or signs of forced entry, even minor ones, may indicate unauthorized access; on their own, they do not prove that someone is still on board.
A broken cargo compartment lock may reveal unauthorized access: it is a sign to investigate, not proof that a person is present.
The company organizes control and reporting procedures and communicates them to drivers: leaving drivers without guidance undermines the security system.
Padlocks and seals help protect the cargo compartment against unauthorized access; they should be checked for signs of tampering.
Suspicions should be reported to the authorities; immediately abandoning the vehicle is not the recommended procedure. Do not approach anyone who may be hiding on board.
Ten minutes is not a safe threshold: even a short unattended stop can allow someone to gain access. The vehicle must be secured and checked.

During specific operations against irregular immigration, when there are reasonable grounds, police may inspect vehicles and the goods they carry even if they are subject to a special customs regime. This power is subject to conditions and territorial limits.
Confronting an armed robber can put your life in danger. Protect yourself and notify the police as soon as you can do so safely.
The police can intervene and gather useful evidence: notify them as soon as you can do so safely.
Police intervention should not be ruled out: reporting the incident allows emergency assistance to be called and information about what happened to be gathered.
Vehicles and loads are targets of crime in road transport: protecting both and choosing safe places to stop reduces exposure to risk.
An alarm or immobilizer adds a barrier against vehicle theft; it should be activated when the vehicle is unattended.
Isolated and poorly lit areas offer less surveillance and make it easier to act unnoticed. For stops, it is preferable to choose safe, well-lit and busy areas.
The driver can also be robbed during transport: property is not worth the risk of confronting the attackers.
The quiz considers the claim that kidnappings are frequent to be false: they are exceptional events, not an ordinary feature of passenger transport. This does not rule out isolated incidents.
Guarded areas are chosen precisely to protect the driver and the load; the risk particularly concerns stops in unsecured areas. Guarding reduces the risk without eliminating it.

The quiz rejects the theft of the engine as the most common purpose of robberies. A documented risk in road transport is instead the theft of goods from the vehicle; the precise comparison of frequencies depends on the available data.
Knowing the locations of risk helps you plan the route and stops in safer areas before setting off.
An isolated place offers less surveillance: when possible, choose a safe place that is not secluded for your stop.
A well-lit area makes people and activities more visible; together with surveillance and other protections, it helps you choose a safer place to stop.
Avoiding a violent response reduces the risk of escalation for the driver and passengers. You can still ask for help and report the behavior.

Preventing robberies does not automatically authorize you to carry a weapon: carrying one outside the home is subject to restrictions and permits. Displaying it on the dashboard is not a standard security measure.
A place that is not isolated offers more opportunities for surveillance; it is also preferable to choose a well-lit and protected area.
Responding violently to provocation can worsen the conflict. Stay calm and seek help if necessary.
The time, place, manner of the incident and useful descriptions help the police reconstruct what happened and investigate.
Avoiding isolated areas whenever possible is a precaution: in a busy place, it is easier to call for help in the event of an assault.
Studying the journey in advance allows you to choose safer routes and places to stop.
The risk of an attack does not authorize exceeding speed limits: they must be respected even in high-risk areas.
A guarded parking area offers greater protection to the driver and the vehicle during a stop.
Using weapons is not permitted in every case: legitimate self-defense requires, among other things, an immediate danger and a defense proportionate to the attack.
Stopping in a busy place makes it easier to call for help and may discourage a robbery, without eliminating the risk.
A crime report must be filed with the judicial authority or the judicial police; notifying the insurance company does not replace it.

Driving and rest times cannot be ignored to arrive sooner. A limited exception is provided for reaching a suitable stopping place and protecting people, the vehicle or the load, without compromising road safety.
Stopping in isolated or dark places increases vulnerability: it is preferable to choose safe, well-lit and busy areas.
Wheel chocks prevent the vehicle from moving accidentally; they are not an anti-theft system. Suitable security devices are needed to deter theft.
The parking brake prevents the vehicle from moving, but it does not protect the load from theft: the cargo compartment must also be closed and secured.
Removing the key and keeping it safe when leaving the vehicle makes it harder to start and steal.
A place with few people around can make things easier for thieves; hazard lights are not an anti-theft device. A safe area is preferable for a stop.
Checking that the cargo compartment is closed makes it harder for unauthorized people to access the goods.
On-time deliveries demonstrate reliability and contribute to customers' assessment of the company.
A company's image encompasses impressions of it and can influence customers' trust and judgment.
A good image can encourage customers to choose the company and remain loyal, and can affect turnover, which also depends on other factors.
Employees' opinions can also contribute to the company's image by conveying their experience of working there.
It is false that road transport is free from competition: looking after its image can help a company stand out and gain customers' trust.
Modern vehicles can contribute to the company's image, for example by giving the impression that it pays attention to service quality.
The type of products carried does not by itself determine the company's image: how the service is provided and how the vehicles are maintained also matter.
The behavior of drivers who interact with customers affects how the service is judged and therefore the company's image.
How a driver presents themselves to customers contributes to their impression of the company the driver represents.
The ability to interact with clients is part of the driver's performance and can influence the company's image.

The quiz considers it false that smoking during a stop by itself determines a company's image. Behavior visible to customers can still influence their impression; the overall way the service is provided matters.
It is false that image is shaped only by advertising: service quality and drivers' behavior also matter.

The type of collective agreement does not by itself determine the company's image: the service and the company's conduct also matter. Working conditions can still influence judgments about the company.
The number of leased vehicles does not by itself determine the company's image: service quality and care of the vehicles also matter.
Taking concrete action to protect the environment can contribute to the company's image by showing responsibility in providing the service.
Improving and renewing the service can strengthen the company's image by showing attention to customers' needs.
It is false that the driver's appearance is irrelevant: neat and appropriate clothing contributes to the company's professional image.
Service quality affects customers' experience and therefore their judgment of the company.
A company's image includes the perceptions and opinions that customers form about it.
It is false that drivers' work has no effect on the company's image: the quality of their performance contributes to how the company is judged.
The driver's nationality does not determine the company's image: what matters is the quality of the service and the professionalism with which it is provided.
Clean, well-maintained vehicles contribute to the perceived quality of the service and the company's image.
The driver represents the company when interacting with passengers: courtesy and communication skills contribute to its image.
It is false that drivers' behavior is irrelevant: how they work and interact with others affects the company's image.
The drivers' age does not determine the company's image: the quality of their performance is what matters.
The driver's performance is part of the service offered, and its quality contributes to the company's image.
It is false that the sector is free from competition: looking after its image can help a company be chosen by customers.
Giving timely notice allows the company to arrange a replacement and ensure the service continues. For illness, the method and timing of notification depend on the employment contract.
Mediating over the price is not automatically the driver's responsibility: the commercial dispute should be referred to those in charge at the company.
The driver may interact with various parties during transport, including customs authorities when they are involved in the operations.
An employed driver is not required, by virtue of that role, to invest personal money in the company: their commitment concerns the work they perform.

The quiz considers the reference to the authorities that issue authorizations false: the driver's contacts normally involve the operational parties involved in transport. Occasional contact with those authorities is still possible.
The driver should not take the employer's side in the price dispute: they should behave professionally and refer the matter to the company.
Even when faced with criticism about the price, the driver represents the company and must behave properly and professionally.
Clothing appropriate for the service contributes to the company's professional image; any specific requirements depend on company rules.
The price dispute concerns the business relationship between the carrier and the customer: the driver is not automatically required to take sides.
While performing the service, the driver may deal with various people, such as freight forwarders in goods transport or travel agents in passenger transport.
Debt collection is not an ordinary duty of a driver: it concerns the company's administration, unless specifically assigned.
Transport carried out with attention to safety protects people and goods and contributes to the quality of the service.
Keeping accounting records is not an ordinary duty of a driver: it concerns administration, unless specifically assigned.
Perfect knowledge of four languages is not generally required: any language skills needed depend on the service and the assignment.
Punctuality helps maintain work arrangements and meet service commitments: the driver must report at the scheduled time.
The driver also represents the company when dealing with customers: their conduct and the quality of their work affect the company's image.
In the quiz, banks are not considered among the people or organizations a driver typically deals with: work contacts include customers. Contact with a bank may nevertheless occur in particular cases.
Courtesy and respect in dealings with customers improve the perceived quality of the service and reflect positively on the company.
A disagreement over the price does not require the driver to take time off work: the commercial issue concerns the carrier and the customer.

It is false that a driver must take out a life insurance policy on their own life to carry out the job. Life cover may be a personal choice or provided for by specific agreements; it is separate from professional qualification and any compulsory insurance applicable to the vehicle or work.
Selecting staff is not an ordinary duty of a driver: the company handles it, unless it is specifically assigned to the driver.
An employed driver must follow instructions issued by the company and superiors concerning the performance and discipline of work, provided those instructions are lawful.
Determining the cost of the service is not an ordinary duty of a driver: it is a management decision for the company, unless specifically assigned.
Promptly reporting problems encountered to the company makes it possible to coordinate responses and limit the consequences for the service.
Having carried out the transport does not oblige the driver to deal directly with the price dispute: the issue concerns the carrier and the customer, unless the driver is specifically assigned to it.
Cooperating with colleagues helps coordinate work and ensures the smooth delivery of the service.
Loyalty requires an employee not to compete with the employer or disclose or use company information in a way that harms the company.
Dealing with unexpected events in accordance with company instructions helps complete the service and meet commitments made to the customer.
Setting up new services on their own initiative is not an ordinary duty of an employed driver: organizing services is the company's responsibility, unless specifically assigned.
The price dispute concerns the carrier and the customer; the driver normally does not deal with it on their own initiative. The driver may still report the facts or intervene if assigned to do so.

The quiz considers it false that believing the customer is right is enough to intervene in price negotiations: the issue concerns the carrier and the customer. The driver may still report the facts or act if assigned to do so.
Diligence requires an employed driver to carry out assigned duties carefully, taking into account their nature and the company's interests.
A vehicle in good working order reduces the risk of breakdowns or faulty equipment compromising safety during transport.
Keeping the vehicle in good working order helps keep pollutant emissions within the prescribed limits.
Keeping the vehicle in good working order is not required to avoid reports to the Chamber of Commerce: it serves to ensure safety and limit noise and pollution.
A vehicle in good working order helps keep noise within the prescribed limits, including through the proper operation of its equipment.
Keeping the vehicle in good working order does not automatically result in a lower insurance premium: it is necessary for safety and to limit noise and pollution.
Keeping the vehicle in good working order is not required to avoid reports to the Register's central committee: it serves to ensure safety and limit noise and pollution.
A visual inspection of the tires can reveal visible cuts and tears.
Looking under the vehicle can reveal visible traces of oil or oil leaks.
Maintenance primarily serves the safety and proper operation of the vehicle, not the prevention of wear on the digital tachograph.
By switching on the lights and observing them, including with another person's help, a driver can identify a lamp that is not working.
The percentage of carbon monoxide cannot be determined by looking at the exhaust fumes: an exhaust gas analyzer is needed.
Oil viscosity cannot be measured by sight: it is determined with an instrument, such as a viscometer.
Recognizing a fault early makes it possible to take action before it worsens or causes further damage.
A navigation system fault alone does not require the driver to stop immediately: the driver must nevertheless continue to drive safely.
Knowing the instruments and warning lights enables the driver to interpret their indications and recognize any faults.
The manual explains the controls and the inspection and maintenance operations specific to the vehicle; the driver must know how to consult it.
Braking is unbalanced when the braking forces of the wheels on the same axle differ significantly.
The quiz considers this case true: different tire pressures can cause the wheels to respond unevenly under braking. This concerns the vehicle's behavior, not necessarily a brake defect.
An unevenly worn disc or drum can impair contact with the braking material and reduce braking effectiveness.
Excessive pedal play does not in itself indicate an imbalance between the wheels: imbalance concerns the difference in braking force on the same axle.
Pressing the pedal too hard does not in itself cause an imbalance between the brakes: this is assessed by comparing the forces of the wheels on the same axle.
Failure of the indicator alone does not directly reduce braking force, but it may prevent a pressure problem from being detected.
Unevenly worn brake linings on the same axle may be associated with unequal braking forces. The cause of the wear, such as a seized caliper, should also be checked.
Severe wear of brake linings, drums or discs damages the braking surfaces and can reduce braking effectiveness.
Having the transmission in neutral does not in itself cause an imbalance between the brakes on the wheels of the same axle; however, in neutral there is no contribution from engine braking.
A clogged particulate filter concerns the exhaust system and is not in itself a service brake defect. Ineffective braking can instead result from wear of the braking surfaces.
A low oil level in the sump concerns engine lubrication and is not in itself a brake fault. A defect in the braking system can, however, reduce braking effectiveness.
A visual check can reveal component defects, but it cannot measure braking efficiency: a braking test using suitable equipment is required.
Oil on braking surfaces can also contaminate the brake linings, reducing friction and therefore braking effectiveness.

The quiz indicates FALSO: steering shimmy is commonly associated with wheel imbalance. The wording is debatable, however: wheel geometry and suspension should also be checked if the vibration persists.

The quiz considers damage to the transmission joint FALSO: steering while stationary mainly stresses the tires and steering components. The connection to a transmission joint nevertheless depends on the vehicle's design.
When the vehicle is stationary, the tires must turn against friction with the ground: repeating the maneuver stresses the steering and can accelerate wear and play in its components.
Excessive play is a loss of steering precision: it does not mean that the front suspension stops working. The two systems have connected components and should nevertheless be checked.
An incorrect wheel alignment angle can make steering harder: for example, excessive caster increases the effort required.
An imbalance in the steered wheels can produce oscillations felt at the steering wheel; the wheel balance should be checked.
Overloading the rear axle is not the typical cause given for stiff steering. Instead, the front tire pressure and steering components, among other things, should be checked.

The quiz marks this false: incorrect pressure is not a definitive diagnosis of the vibration; wheel balance and steering components should also be checked. However, the wording is absolute: in practice, incorrect pressure can also contribute to tire irregularities and should be checked.
Working power steering reduces the effort needed to turn the wheel; a malfunction in it can make the steering stiff.
Incorrect toe adjustment can contribute to deviation from a straight path; the wheel alignment should be checked.
The quiz marks this false: a noncompliant size does not in itself imply vibration. One possible cause is imbalance of the wheel and tire assembly; the sizes must nevertheless be those permitted.
Play is movement of the steering wheel that does not yet move the wheels. If excessive, it compromises precision and should be checked periodically.

The quiz marks this false: excessive wear alone does not necessarily identify the cause of vibration. However, irregular wear or a deformed tire can be accompanied by vibration and require inspection.
Vibration can be a symptom of a fault in the steering components; it should be checked along with the wheels and suspension.
The universal joint on the drive shaft transmits motion to the driven wheels; steering play concerns the connection between the steering wheel and the steered wheels.

In hydraulic power steering systems, the fluid level should be checked periodically according to the manufacturer's instructions. This check does not apply to a fully electric power steering system without a reservoir.
Excessive play mainly compromises directional precision; it does not necessarily cause premature wear of the rear tires.
If the power steering assistance is not working properly, turning the steering wheel may require more effort.
Insufficient pressure in the front tires can increase the effort needed to steer; the prescribed pressure should be restored.
When steering while stationary, the friction between the tires and the ground must be overcome; the increased stress can wear the steering components.
VERO. An excessive load on the front axle increases the effort needed to steer the wheels and can make the steering stiffer. The load distribution and limits should be checked.
Insufficient pressure can make the steering stiffer, but it does not create mechanical play between the steering wheel and the wheels: its cause should be sought in the steering components.
The typical cause of stiff steering is insufficient front tire pressure, not excessive pressure. The pressure should nevertheless be maintained at the prescribed value.
Excessive play in the steering controls or joints can contribute to oscillations felt at the steering wheel; their condition should be checked.
Holding the steering wheel firmly does not eliminate mechanical play: the fault must be identified and corrected in the steering components.
With too much play, the steering wheel moves through part of its travel without controlling the wheels: corrections are less precise and it becomes harder to follow the intended path.
The axle shafts transmit driving force; steering play concerns the components connecting the steering wheel to the steered wheels, and its cause should be sought there.
An unbalanced front wheel can generate vibrations that are transmitted to the steering, causing it to shimmy.
The alternator is not connected directly only to the headlights: it supplies the vehicle's electrical system and recharges the battery; the headlights are electrical loads on their circuit.
An incorrectly fitted bulb may be out of its intended position in the headlight assembly and alter the direction of the light beam.
If the device that adjusts the headlight's angle is damaged, the beam may remain incorrectly aimed.

A faulty fuse can interrupt the light's power supply, but it is not the usual cause of a lit beam being aimed incorrectly. In systems with electric adjustment, the adjuster's circuit should also be checked.

Connecting the two terminals of the same battery to each other causes a dangerous short circuit; it does not start the engine. Instead, the cause of the failure to start should be checked and the manufacturer's procedure followed.
Periodically checking that the terminal clamps are tight helps maintain a good electrical connection: loose clamps can cause poor contact.
Hazard lights warn of danger; they do not repair the headlights or replace their illumination of the road.
A faulty indicator light can give the driver an incorrect indication, but it does not in itself change the headlight's aim, which depends on its adjustment and optical assembly.

The quiz distinguishes aim from light output: slight oxidation of the reflector can reduce or alter the reflected light, but it is not the same as incorrect headlight adjustment. Deterioration of the optical assembly can nevertheless change the distribution of light.
If the headlight has not been adjusted correctly, its beam may point too high, too low or to the side.
A damaged fuse can interrupt the power supply circuit and prevent the headlights from working.
The rectifier does not compensate for weight imbalances: in the alternator, it converts the alternating current produced into direct current for the electrical system.
Clearance lights indicate the vehicle's presence and width; they do not repair the headlights or replace their beam for illuminating the road.
In vehicles equipped with bulb monitoring, an indicator light or dashboard message can signal a headlight failure.

Sufficient tread depth does not permit different types of tires on the same axle: those normally fitted on the same axle must be of the same type, subject to the specific exceptions provided for a temporary spare wheel.
Potholes and impacts on a rough road can damage the tire's casing or other parts; it is advisable to check it after the journey.

A loss of wheel balance mainly causes vibration; a tendency to pull to one side can instead be due, for example, to incorrect alignment or different tire pressures. The symptoms should nevertheless be investigated.
Incorrect toe adjustment can cause the tires to run at an incorrect angle and produce irregular tread wear.
Incorrect pressure can worsen steering response and stability, especially when cornering. It should therefore be checked frequently against the values prescribed for the vehicle and load.
The tread wears with use: periodic checks help detect wear and abnormalities before they compromise the tire's effectiveness.
Incorrect toe adjustment does not reduce the risk of skidding: it can worsen the vehicle's ability to hold its path and its response, as well as cause irregular tire wear.
For motor vehicles, trolleybuses and trailers, the main grooves must be at least 1.6 mm deep. The question does not specify the vehicle: different limits apply to motorcycles and mopeds.
Insufficient pressure tends to wear mainly the shoulders of the tread, not its center; wear in the center is typically associated with excessive pressure.
Poor wheel balance is not a way to reduce braking distance: it can cause vibration and irregular wear and should be corrected.
Pressure different from the prescribed value can accelerate tread wear and make it irregular; it should be checked periodically when the tires are cold.
The 6 mm limit is incorrect: for motor vehicles and trailers, the main grooves must be at least 1.6 mm deep.
When steering while stationary, the tread scrubs against the ground: repeating the maneuver can contribute to abnormal tire wear.
It is incorrect to attribute wear at the sides to excessive pressure: this tends to wear mainly the center; insufficient pressure contributes to wear on the shoulders.
When the vehicle is stationary, the wheels turn against friction with the ground: the strain can damage the tyres.
Shock absorbers act on suspension oscillations, not on the operation of the differential. When worn out, they mainly impair stability and control.
Shock absorbers dampen suspension oscillations: their wear does not directly affect the operation of the gearbox, but it can impair stability and control.
Worn shock absorbers can reach the end of their travel and cause knocks over bumps, increasing vehicle noise.
Effective suspension helps maintain wheel contact and vehicle control, so its effectiveness also affects grip when cornering.
Worn-out shock absorbers dampen oscillations less effectively, making the vehicle's handling less stable and precise.
Open windows are not a normal cause of mechanical instability: this can be caused, for example, by ineffective suspension or shock absorbers.
Stability also depends on the position of the load: a high centre of gravity or a poorly distributed load can make the vehicle less stable.
Damaged leaf springs or springs alter the vehicle's support and alignment and can therefore impair its stability while driving.
Porous asphalt is not in itself a cause of instability: it helps drain surface water. Actual road conditions and speed remain important, however.
Shock absorbers dampen the movement of the springs: if they are worn out, the vehicle body can continue to oscillate abnormally.
A fault in the air suspension adjustment system can alter the vehicle's height and alignment and impair its stability.
It is wrong to plug the exhaust with polystyrene: the exhaust must not be obstructed, and the required silencer must be kept effective and unmodified.
The quiz indicates VERO: worn rings can allow oil into the combustion chamber. The colour is ambiguous, however: burning oil typically produces bluish smoke, not necessarily white.
The quiz indicates FALSO in reference to exhaust emissions: tyre wear is not a direct cause of engine fumes. More broadly, however, tyre wear produces non-exhaust particulate matter.
The quiz indicates VERO: oil entering the combustion chamber can burn and produce polluting smoke. The colour, however, is often bluish and does not by itself identify the cause.
In the context of the quiz, gearbox wear is not a direct cause of increased exhaust emissions; the engine and fuel system should be checked instead.
The quiz indicates FALSO, but the statement is technically ambiguous: in diesel engines, poor atomisation due to faulty injectors can cause white or grey smoke from unburnt fuel.
A poorly adjusted injection pump can alter the quantity or timing of fuel delivery and increase engine emissions.
The required silencer must be compliant and kept in effective working order to limit exhaust noise.
If the silencer is damaged, it reduces exhaust gas noise less effectively and the vehicle can become noisier.
FALSO. Inserting steel wool is not necessary: exhaust noise is reduced with an intact, properly maintained silencer.
VERO. A clogged air filter restricts the air drawn in and can contribute to incomplete combustion and increased smoke.
VERO according to the quiz: worn rings can allow oil into the chamber, where it burns. The colour is imprecise, however: smoke from oil is normally bluish.
FALSO. A clogged oil filter is not the typical cause identified: black smoke can result from incomplete combustion, for example due to a clogged air filter.
FALSO. A lack of coolant concerns the cooling system; black smoke, on the other hand, is associated with combustion problems, such as a clogged air filter.

The quiz indicates FALSO, but the wording is questionable: delayed injection can increase white smoke when the engine is cold. Colour alone neither identifies the cause nor demonstrates how polluting the exhaust is.
FALSO according to the quiz: a clogged air filter is typically associated with black smoke due to insufficient air. Colour alone, however, does not allow a certain diagnosis.
VERO according to the quiz: an out-of-round cylinder can impair the seal of the rings and cause oil to burn. Describing the smoke as white is imprecise: burning oil typically produces bluish smoke.
VERO. A clogged air filter restricts air intake and can contribute to incomplete combustion and black smoke.
VERO according to the quiz: worn oil control rings can allow oil to enter the chamber and burn. Smoke from oil is normally bluish, however, not necessarily white.
FALSO. The alternator produces electrical power; black smoke, on the other hand, is connected with combustion, for example an insufficient air supply.
VERO. Faulty or poorly adjusted injectors alter fuel delivery and can increase exhaust smoke.
FALSO. Antifreeze is used in the cooling system, not to silence the vehicle; exhaust noise is controlled with an effective silencer.
FALSO according to the quiz, in reference to exhaust emissions: brakes do not control combustion. The wording is generic, however: brake wear also produces non-exhaust particulate matter.
VERO. Squealing brakes are a source of noise: the fault in the braking components must be checked and corrected.
VERO. A damaged pressure plate can exert insufficient pressure on the disc, causing it to slip.
FALSO. A lack of oil in the gearbox is not the typical cause of slipping: the clutch disc, pressure plate and clutch control should be checked instead.
FALSO. Running in alone does not cause slipping: a properly functioning clutch transmits torque even before it is fully run in; slipping indicates a fault or unsuitable conditions.
VERO. A disc with worn friction linings may no longer transmit torque properly and may slip.
VERO. Oil on the linings reduces friction and can cause the clutch to slip.
FALSO. Poor balance mainly causes vibrations; slipping results from insufficient ability to transmit torque, as with worn or oily linings.
FALSO. Noise from the shock absorbers concerns the suspension and does not in itself indicate an engine fault; overheating coolant is one possible sign of an engine problem.
VERO. Overheating coolant can signal a cooling system problem and therefore abnormal engine operation.
FALSO. The differential is part of the transmission: a fault in it does not in itself demonstrate abnormal engine operation. Overheating coolant, on the other hand, is one possible sign.
FALSO. The tachograph records driving data, and a fault in it does not in itself indicate an engine defect; overheating coolant, on the other hand, is one possible sign.
An irregular idle can signal abnormal engine operation, for example an ignition fault.
Detonation is abnormal combustion that can manifest itself as knocking in the engine.

The quiz considers it false that damage is acceptable simply because it is minor: the glass must ensure visibility and safety. The seriousness of damage also depends on its location and its effect on visibility.
The windscreen must be kept in a condition that ensures the best possible visibility, even in rain or when fogged up; extreme conditions can nevertheless reduce visibility.
Clean windows make it easier to see the road: dirt and smears can obstruct the view.
Lubricating oil is not a glass cleaner and can leave a film that obstructs the view. Products suitable for cleaning glass should be used.
A properly functioning windscreen wiper removes water and dirt from the windscreen, helping to maintain visibility.
Sand must not be added to the windscreen washer: an appropriate fluid capable of cleaning the windscreen should be used.
It is wrong to fit non-compliant glass: replacement requires approved safety glass suitable for the vehicle.
Undamaged glass helps maintain visibility and safety. During an inspection, the assessment of damage also depends on its position and its effect on the view.
Checking the washer fluid level helps ensure fluid is available to clean the windscreen while driving.
Safety glass must be of a compliant type approved for use on the vehicle.
Applying film to the windscreen does not guarantee better visibility: it can reduce transparency or obstruct the view.
After starting the engine, check that the malfunction warning lights go out: a light that stays on may indicate a fault. Some come on temporarily for the initial check.
Cold alone is not the cause indicated by the alternator warning light: with the engine running, it signals a problem with the charging system that needs to be checked.
The oil pressure warning light concerns lubrication, not the fluidity of the coolant. It may come on if the oil pressure is insufficient.
The warning light indicates an excessive coolant temperature, not its pressure directly. Pressure and temperature can nevertheless be related.
If the belt drives the coolant pump, a broken belt can interrupt coolant circulation and cause overheating.
Insufficient oil can cause the pressure to drop and the corresponding warning light to come on.
A fault in the sensor or measuring circuit can cause the warning light to come on even without actual overheating: the cause must be checked.
The quiz marks this false, but the wording is debatable: an excessive load can contribute to overheating and therefore cause the warning light to come on.
The warning light concerns the engine coolant temperature, not the operation of the cabin demisting system.
A fault in the rectifier diodes can impair charging and cause the alternator warning light to come on.
A faulty oil pump can cause insufficient pressure and bring on the warning light; the light alone does not identify the faulty component.

The quiz marks this false: the warning light measures coolant temperature, whereas a lack of oil primarily concerns lubrication. The wording is nevertheless ambiguous because a severe shortage of oil can indirectly contribute to overheating.
A faulty fan can reduce cooling of the radiator: the coolant overheats and the warning light may come on.

Driving along a long straight road at a constant speed does not in itself cause the warning light to come on: it indicates an excessive temperature, which must be traced to the conditions or a cooling system fault.

Using intended electrical equipment at the same time does not in itself indicate an alternator fault: the warning light signals a charging problem. An excessive load or an actual fault nevertheless requires checking.
The door fuse protects the corresponding circuit; it does not in itself indicate a charging fault. The alternator warning light concerns the charging system.
If the belt driving the alternator breaks, the alternator may stop charging the battery and the warning light may come on.
A blown headlight bulb is not in itself a charging fault: the alternator warning light indicates a possible problem with the charging system.
Knowing the warning lights enables the driver to recognise a fault and take the action specified in the vehicle manual.
If the oil pressure warning light comes on while driving, stop safely, switch off the engine and check the level with the dipstick according to the manual. A correct level does not rule out a fault.

The quiz considers it false to attribute the warning light directly to failure to change the oil: the light normally concerns insufficient pressure, not the oil change interval. However, neglected maintenance can indirectly contribute to lubrication faults; the oil should be changed according to the specified schedule.
A faulty water pump can impair coolant circulation and cause overheating, bringing on the warning light.
The oil in the pneumohydraulic converter is not the engine lubricating oil: the warning light concerns engine oil pressure.
The engine oil warning light may come on when lubrication pressure is insufficient: stop and switch off the engine.
Overheated brakes are not in themselves the cause of the engine coolant warning light: it concerns the temperature of the engine cooling circuit.
A faulty thermostat, for example one stuck closed, can obstruct cooling and cause the coolant to overheat.
With the engine running, the warning light may indicate a fault in the charging system: the alternator might not be charging the battery.

The quiz considers it true that a faulty indication can cause the warning light to come on. A distinction is needed: a fault in the warning circuit can produce an incorrect indication, whereas a bulb that has simply blown may not light up at all.
Insufficient coolant can impair cooling and lead to an excessive temperature: that is why the level is among the first things to check.
Do not increase engine speed or continue driving: if the oil pressure warning light comes on, stop safely as soon as possible and switch off the engine.
Exceeding urban speed limits does not help maintain the vehicle's efficiency: speed limits must be observed.
Changing the transmission oil is part of scheduled maintenance, at the intervals specified for the vehicle and its use.
The oil scraper ring is fitted to the piston: routine adjustment every six months is not prescribed. Work on the rings is carried out as part of an engine repair.
Annual polishing is cosmetic care, not a requirement for mechanical efficiency: what matters is carrying out the maintenance specified by the manufacturer.
Piston rings are not routinely replaced every 10,000 km: they are assessed and replaced when the engine's condition requires work.
Changing the engine oil is a normal scheduled maintenance operation, to be carried out according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Replacing the entire engine is an extraordinary repair, not routine maintenance: the routine schedule instead includes periodic work such as oil changes.
Routine maintenance includes periodic checks of mechanical parts, according to the manufacturer's schedule.
Periodic preventive maintenance helps identify problems and prevent breakdowns during use.
There is no general requirement to wash the oil filter annually: the filter or its element is replaced at the intervals prescribed by the manufacturer.
Replacing the air filter is part of maintenance: it is done according to the instructions applicable to the vehicle and the filter.
There is no universal weekly washing frequency required for efficiency: maintenance follows the vehicle's needs and the manufacturer's instructions.
A worn component may need to be repaired or replaced before it fails, when it reaches the permitted limits.
Belts subject to wear and aging are checked and replaced at the prescribed intervals. The quiz wording contains a typo: it refers to drive belts.
The driver must recognize when a breakdown requires qualified personnel: repairs should be entrusted to appropriately trained people.
Reporting a malfunction promptly allows the company to assess it and arrange for repairs.
It is wrong not to report problems: the driver must communicate any faults detected so they can be assessed and repaired.
The air filter should be checked according to the applicable instructions: if it is too clogged, it restricts the air needed for combustion.
The oil filter does not control coolant temperature: it traps impurities in the lubricating oil and is replaced at the prescribed intervals.
The filter traps particles in the lubricating oil; periodic replacement keeps the filtration effective.
An excessively clogged filter obstructs airflow. It must be kept in working order and replaced when necessary, following the manufacturer's instructions; not all filters can be washed.
The engine air filter is not a cooling device: it filters the air drawn in for combustion.
In disc brakes, the brake pads' friction material is also checked for wear.
The air in a pneumatic system's reservoir is the reserve needed for braking: its mere presence does not reduce braking distance. Insufficient pressure is what impairs braking.
In drum brakes, the inspection includes checking the brake shoe friction linings for wear.
In hydraulic systems, the brake fluid level is checked periodically; the fluid is necessary for the system to operate.
The color of the brake pads is not the specified inspection criterion: the condition and thickness of the friction material are the main things checked.
It is wrong to exclude brake fluid: in vehicles equipped with it, both its level and the engine oil level are checked.
Brake shoe effectiveness is not checked simply by measuring hardness: in particular, the friction lining is checked for wear.

VERO. In hydraulic braking systems, the brake fluid level in the relevant reservoir is checked periodically. The term ‘brake booster oil’ is imprecise: the check and the fluid depend on the type of system specified by the manufacturer.
A leak in the pneumatic system can cause the pressure in the reservoirs to drop; the fault requires inspection.

Water occupies part of the tank, leaving less volume for compressed air: when the same amount of air is drawn off, the pressure can change more quickly, moving the needle. This is a possible physical explanation, not a definite diagnosis of the fault.
FALSO. The pneumatic system operates the brakes with compressed air: checking the brake fluid concerns any hydraulic section, not the air reservoir.
FALSO. The percentage of carbon dioxide is not checked: instead, the pressure and leak-tightness of the compressed-air circuit are checked.
FALSO. The lubricating oil dipstick does not check the brakes: in the hydraulic section, the brake fluid level is checked in the relevant reservoir.
VERO. Accumulated water occupies part of the reservoir, reducing the volume available for compressed air; it must be removed using the prescribed draining procedure.
FALSO. A water level is not checked: in the hydraulic section, the level of the prescribed brake fluid is checked.
VERO. The pipes must be leak-tight: a leak reduces the air reserve needed for braking.
VERO. The air reservoirs must be checked for integrity and secure mounting because they hold the reserve for the brakes.
FALSO. The duplex valve controls air pressure in the two pneumatic circuits; the brake fluid level concerns any hydraulic section.
VERO. Brake linings wear down: checking their thickness makes it possible to identify those that need replacing.
FALSO. Infrequent use of the brakes does not normally cause excessive pressure: the regulator stops charging at the specified pressure; any excess indicates a fault.
FALSO. In a pneumatic system, the air circuit is checked for leaks, not a hydraulic pump; the latter belongs to any hydraulic section.
FALSO. Water does not increase the volume available for air: it occupies part of the reservoir and must be drained according to the instructions.
VERO. An abnormal pressure drop may indicate a leak: the system, including the pipes, must be checked and the fault repaired before setting off again.
VERO. The linings of brake shoes or pads are subject to wear and must be inspected to determine whether replacement is needed.
FALSO. Prolonged use of the brakes does not normally cause excessive pressure in the reservoir: braking consumes air, while the regulator controls the charging pressure.
VERO. In a pneumatic-hydraulic system, the brake fluid level in the hydraulic section's reservoir must also be checked, according to the vehicle's instructions.
FALSO. The specified periodic check for the hydraulic circuit concerns the brake fluid level, not measurement of its viscosity.
FALSO. Checking the gearbox casing is not enough to check the clutch: its components and, where specified, the pedal free play are checked instead.
VERO. The clutch disc lining wears down; excessive wear can cause slipping and requires inspection.
FALSO. The disc temperature is not the ordinary periodic check required by the question: wear and control free play are checked instead, depending on the type of clutch.
VERO. Where the type of control calls for it, the pedal's free play must be checked: clutch wear can reduce it and require adjustment.
VERO. The correct gearbox oil level ensures lubrication of its components; it must be checked according to the manufacturer's schedule.
VERO. Checking the gearbox oil level helps keep the gears lubricated and prevent wear and damage.
FALSO. Gearbox oil lubricates the gearbox components; it does not make the clutch, which has its own control, operate more smoothly.
FALSO. Water must not be added to differential oil: it contaminates the oil and can cause corrosion and damage. Use the lubricant prescribed for the vehicle.
The universal joint has no oil level to check: depending on its type, it may require greasing or may already be lubricated.

The quiz distinguishes the clutch from the gearbox: pedal free play concerns the clutch, while the gearbox is also assessed by how the gears engage. The distinction is not absolute: a poorly adjusted clutch can make gear engagement difficult.
Unusual noises during gear engagement may indicate a gearbox problem and warrant inspection.
Leaks from brake pipes concern the braking system, not gearbox performance; gear engagement is also observed when assessing the gearbox.
A flexible coupling generally has no oil level to check; maintenance depends on the type of coupling and the manufacturer's instructions.
Differential oil lubricates the differential gears, not the engine lubrication system, which has its own oil.
Differential oil lubricates its gears, including the spider and side gears; the level must be checked according to the vehicle's specifications.
Gearbox oil serves the gearbox; it does not check the engine's timing components. For those, the timing belt is checked, if fitted.
The camshaft operates the valves and must be properly lubricated to limit wear on the timing components.
The timing belt, when fitted, synchronizes the crankshaft and camshaft; inspection and replacement follow the manufacturer's schedule.
Transmission lubrication concerns the components that transmit motion to the wheels; it does not check the engine timing system, for which the belt is also checked if fitted.
Checking the coolant helps keep the cooling system effective and prevent overheating, not prevent an excessive drop in oil temperature.
A sufficient coolant level is necessary for the cooling circuit to work and must be checked periodically according to the manual.
FALSO. An engine can start and the vehicle can move off before the engine reaches operating temperature; cold can, however, make starting more difficult.
An insufficient coolant level can impair heat dissipation and contribute to engine overheating.

The quiz assumes water is added to an already correct mixture: diluting it too much reduces frost protection. The statement is general: the result depends on the initial concentration; the prescribed mixture should be used.
The cabin temperature is not enough to check engine cooling: instead, the coolant level and circuit components are checked. Insufficient heating can nevertheless be a useful symptom.
The air filter concerns the engine's air intake; it is not a check of the cooling circuit. Instead, the coolant and circuit components are checked.
The electric fan helps air flow through the radiator; if it does not operate correctly, the engine may overheat.
The filter traps impurities and, if it is not replaced at the specified intervals, can accumulate debris until it becomes clogged.
The correct oil level ensures engine lubrication; insufficient oil can cause serious damage due to a lack of lubrication.
A clogged filter may no longer trap impurities effectively and, if the bypass valve opens, oil may circulate without being filtered. Impurities also cause clogging.
Periodic internal inspection of the cartridge is not required: the filter is replaced at the prescribed intervals; the oil level is checked using the system provided by the vehicle.
In engines fitted with a dipstick, the level is checked by comparing the oil mark with the notches, following the vehicle's instructions.
A very dirty filter can contribute to insufficient oil pressure: inadequate lubrication can damage pistons and cylinders. The presence of a bypass valve changes how the circuit behaves.
FALSO. The oil filter concerns lubrication: if clogged, it can increase engine wear. Black smoke, on the other hand, is associated with combustion problems, for example insufficient air intake.
FALSO. The oil filter belongs to the engine lubrication system; a clogged filter can damage the engine, but is not a brake booster fault.
FALSO. The oil level is checked to ensure lubrication and protect the engine from wear, not to prevent it from over-revving.

The official verdict is FALSO: in systems with a working bypass, if the filter becomes clogged, the valve allows oil to flow around it. The wording is absolute, however: a bypass failure or a different configuration can compromise lubrication.

FALSO. Checking engine oil periodically is good maintenance practice in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions, but the question incorrectly attributes a specific requirement for periodic level checks to the Highway Code.

The mileage at the previous oil change is used to compare the distance driven with the manufacturer's specified maintenance interval; on its own, it does not prove that the entire system is working correctly.
FALSO. The electric fan serves the cooling system, not to check lubrication. For lubrication, the oil and its system are checked according to the manufacturer's instructions.
FALSO. The air filter concerns the engine's air intake: if clogged, it can reduce engine performance, but does not in itself make the brakes ineffective.
VERO. In engines fitted with an injection pump, checking it is part of fuel system maintenance, according to the manufacturer's instructions and by qualified personnel.

FALSO. A clogged fuel filter mainly restricts fuel supply; injector wear is associated with contaminants reaching the injectors. A damaged filter or one that lets impurities through can nevertheless compromise injection.
FALSO. A clogged air filter restricts air intake and can be associated with black smoke, not specifically white smoke.
A clogged filter obstructs airflow; clogging itself does not cause impurities to enter. Unfiltered air can, however, enter because of a damaged filter or a faulty seal.
The pollen filter concerns cabin air, not the air drawn into the engine: if clogged, it reduces interior ventilation, not vehicle performance directly.
FALSO. A clogged fuel filter restricts fuel supply and can reduce power or stop the engine; black smoke is not the characteristic consequence indicated by the quiz.
FALSO. The water pump belongs to the cooling system. For the fuel system, the components that deliver and meter fuel are checked instead.
A clogged fuel filter restricts fuel supply and can reduce engine performance.
A clogged air filter limits the air available for combustion and can alter it; the actual effect depends on the engine and its management system.
A clogged cabin filter reduces air exchange and can contribute to dampness and unpleasant odors, worsening the quality of the air inside.
If the filter is on the suction side of the pump, clogging obstructs the flow of fuel and can make the supply insufficient or irregular.
The air filter must be checked because it ensures that clean air reaches the engine; if clogged, it can reduce airflow and performance.
A clogged air filter can reduce the air available and contribute to black smoke, especially in a diesel engine; this does not necessarily happen in every engine.
Clogging restricts the air drawn in and can reduce engine power and efficiency.
The oil pump concerns lubrication, not fuel supply. For the latter, the components that carry fuel to the engine, such as the fuel pump, are checked instead.
FALSO. A clogged fuel filter restricts fuel supply; cylinder lubrication depends on the oil system.
The fuel filter traps particles and other impurities, protecting the injection system.
The starter motor brushes ensure electrical contact: if worn or stuck, they can prevent effective starting. They should be checked according to the prescribed maintenance schedule.
The bevel gear set belongs to the transmission, not the starting circuit. For the latter, the battery, connections and starter motor are checked instead.
Loose or corroded terminals obstruct the flow of current needed by the starter motor; the connections must therefore be checked to ensure they are tight.
The fan serves the cooling system and is not the check required for starting. For the starting system, the battery, connections and starter motor are checked.
A fuse protects an electrical circuit: when it blows, the protected circuit is no longer powered. Its failure therefore concerns the electrical system.
The battery supplies electrical equipment and the starting system; checking its state of charge helps identify electrical system problems.
A fuse protects an electrical circuit; it is not part of the mechanical transmission. Its failure is therefore an electrical fault.
The quiz refers to spark plugs: a diesel engine ignites fuel by compression and does not use them. It may, however, have glow plugs, which are different components.
A faulty fuse interrupts only the circuit it protects: it does not necessarily cause the engine to stop. It can, however, do so if it supplies a system essential to the engine.
The distributor distributes the spark in spark-ignition systems; a diesel engine ignites fuel by compression and does not use this device.
A blown fuse is replaced with one of the same type and specified rating. If the new fuse fails, the cause in the circuit must be identified.
The belt drives the alternator: checking it for wear and replacing it when necessary helps keep the charging system working efficiently.
The alternator powers electrical equipment and charges the battery while the engine is running; checking its operation helps detect charging problems.
If the belt that drives the alternator breaks, the alternator does not turn and does not charge the battery.
The alternator charges the battery while the engine is running: a fault that stops it producing electricity prevents charging.

In the quiz model, the alternator charges the battery and does not directly operate the pneumatic-hydraulic part of the brakes. On vehicles with electronic controls, however, a loss of power can impair their functions.
The warning light does not measure the pressure of the battery fluid: if it stays on while the engine is running, it signals a possible problem with the charging system.

A dynamo is not a battery and is not recharged. The rectifier, on the other hand, is associated with the alternator and converts the current produced to power the electrical system and charge the battery.
The rectifier converts the alternating current produced by the alternator into current suitable for the battery; a fault in it can prevent proper charging.
The pump circulates the coolant; a fault in it does not by itself prevent the alternator from charging. A faulty shared belt can, however, stop both.
If the warning light stays on while the engine is running, it signals a possible charging fault: the battery may not be receiving the correct charge.
The alternator is not the cable that carries current: it produces electricity, powers electrical equipment and charges the battery through the system's connections.
In the quiz model, an alternator fault does not directly affect the pneumatic-hydraulic part of the brakes. A loss of power can, however, make electronic control functions unavailable.
The alternator generates alternating current, which is then rectified to power the electrical system and charge the battery. A fault that interrupts production can prevent charging.
Checking pipes and joints makes it possible to identify cracks, holes or leaks that compromise the exhaust system's seal.
The terminals belong to the electrical system, not the exhaust. For the exhaust, its components are checked, such as the catalytic converter when present.
The catalytic converter, when present, treats exhaust gases: checking its condition is part of verifying the system's efficiency.
Brake shoes are components of the brakes, not the exhaust. For the exhaust, its components are checked instead, such as the catalytic converter when present.
A fire extinguisher is not operated for a routine check: discharging it makes it unavailable. Its condition is checked and maintenance is entrusted to competent personnel.
The driver must make sure that the fire extinguisher is kept in working order and that the periodic checks have been carried out; maintenance is entrusted to competent personnel.
It is not essential for the driver to personally identify the cause of every fault to keep fuel consumption down. The driver must detect and report faults so that they can be checked and repaired.
The driver does not have to sign the document after the inspection: a successful result is certified by a label affixed to the vehicle registration document.
Resetting the engine timing is technical work on the engine, not a skill required of every driver. Any faults should be reported to competent personnel.

The quiz considers it false that a driver can replace brake pads simply by virtue of driving: brakes require suitable skills and equipment. A driver who is also qualified may, however, possess those skills.
The driver must check that the required inspection is valid: driving with an expired inspection entails penalties and suspension from use on the road until the inspection is carried out.
The driver must not personally dismantle a faulty tachograph: repair must be entrusted to an authorized installer or workshop.
The tachograph must undergo the required periodic inspections at an authorized workshop; the driver checks that they have been carried out.
Checking the lights before setting off helps identify any faults that impair visibility and the vehicle's ability to signal its presence.
Bus doors must work properly to allow passengers to board and get off safely: the driver checks them before setting off.
Interior lights, including aisle lights, must be checked to ensure visibility on board and passenger safety.
A discolored area is a cosmetic defect, not the check required before setting off. The bodywork should instead be checked for dangerous or unsecured parts.
Checking whether the lights come on is not reserved for an auto electrician: the driver can check their operation and report any faults.
Windshield washer fluid should be checked and topped up when necessary, because washing helps keep the view clear.
A small business owner is not distinguished by the predominance of capital: the business must be organized predominantly around the owner's and family members' work.
The defining feature is the predominance of the owner's and family's work in the organization of the business, including over the work of any other workers.
The absence of other workers is not necessary: they may be employed, provided the business is organized predominantly around the owner's and family's work.
A transport business is among the activities subject to registration in the business register.
Registration does not concern only those who transport goods on their own account: the requirement for a transport business is not limited to that case.
The PRA concerns vehicles and does not replace the business register: a transport business is subject to registration in the latter.
Registration does not depend on operating internationally: a transport business operating nationally is also subject to registration.
Logistics plans and controls the flow of materials from their origin to the customer, also coordinating the necessary information.
It is false that logistics is limited to the warehouse: it also includes planning and controlling flows and transport through to the customer.
It is false that logistics platforms only store and handle goods: they can also prepare orders and coordinate shipments.
Logistics platforms coordinate operations and flows to make logistics services more efficient and faster.

The quiz considers it false to identify harmonizing shipping costs as the purpose of logistics platforms: their broader purpose is to organize flows efficiently. The statement is ambiguous because cost optimization can nevertheless be an outcome.
Punctuality meets the customer's needs: the shipment must arrive by the expected or agreed deadline.
Logistics organizes flows to meet customer needs, including delivery times.
It is false that logistics is unrelated to these needs: it organizes flows according to production and customer demands, which can change.
False: globalization extends supply chains and makes them more complex, influencing how flows are organized.
False: more frequent deliveries require adjustments to transport and inventory planning.
Globalization influences logistics because it connects suppliers and customers in different markets, requiring international flows to be managed.
Legal protection of consumers is not the specific role of logistics, which organizes flows and deliveries to meet customer needs.
Vehicle maintenance is not the specific issue identified here: logistics mainly coordinates flows, inventory and deliveries. Maintenance can nevertheless support transport reliability.
Logistics plans and coordinates flows to help shipments arrive on schedule.

The quiz considers the quality of the finished product to be false as a specific logistics concern: logistics deals mainly with flows and deliveries. The wording is broad, however: logistics can help preserve quality during storage and transport.
In the distribution channel, several parties coordinate flows so that the requested products reach the market in the right places and at the right times.
Picking consists of selecting and taking from the warehouse the quantities needed to assemble an order, including from different load units.
Picking involves taking the required items from stock and bringing them together to prepare orders for shipment.
False: picking is the retrieval of items to prepare an order; delivery to the recipient is a later stage.
False: an incorrect shipment can leave the customer without the requested products and therefore dissatisfied.

The quiz considers it false that speed is always less important: timely availability also matters to the customer. Its importance relative to price and quality depends on the customer and the product, however.
The logistics system combines resources, facilities and operating rules to manage both goods and the information accompanying their flows.
It is false that the logistics system is the same as the vehicle fleet: it also includes warehouses, resources, information and the organization of flows.
The logistics system includes interdependent activities, such as transport, inventory and warehousing: a decision in one area affects the others.
Coordinating activities as a system makes it possible to assess overall costs and can reduce them by avoiding isolated decisions.
False. Logistics must coordinate with production, marketing and sales: availability and deliveries must meet production schedules and customer demand.
False. The logistics system is integrated, but it includes distinct activities, such as transport, warehousing and order preparation.

True. Using specialized operators can encourage the concentration of resources and flows in shared networks, with economies of scale; this connection does not mean that every outsourcing arrangement produces a merger between companies.

False according to the quiz: outsourcing can help reduce costs and expand or improve services through specialized resources. The wording is ambiguous, however: it is neither the only way to achieve these results nor a guarantee of them.
False. Outsourcing can change operational flexibility, for example by allowing resources to be adjusted to volumes; the effect depends on the contract and the provider.
